test_title: PYST 25: SSC GD Constable - Quantitative Aptitude (Held on: 2nd November 2021 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: A certain sum amounts to ₹9,036 after 3 years and to ₹11484 after 7 years at the same rate per cent per annum at simple interest. What will the compound interest( in ₹) (to the nearest ₹) on the same sum for 2 years at the double rate of interest if interest is compounded annually?
solution:
**Given:**

Amount after 3 years = ₹9,036

Amount after 7 years = ₹11,484

rate of interest = constant

**Formula used:**

S.I = (P × T × R)/100

C.I = P[(1 + R/100)T - 1]

Here, P = Sum, R = Rate, and T = Time

**Calculation:**

Interest received for 4 years = 11484 - 9036 = 2448

So, interest for 3 years = 2448 × (3/4) = 1836

∴ Sum = 9036 - 1836 = 7200

Let the rate of interest be R, therefore

⇒ (7200 × R × 3)/100 = 1836 

⇒ R = 1836/(72 × 3) = 8.5

C.I = 7200[(1 + 17/100)² - 1]

⇒ 7200[(117/100)2 - 1]

⇒ 7200[(13689/10000) - 1]

⇒ 7200[(13689 - 10000)/10000)]

⇒ 7200[3689/10000]

⇒ 2656.08 ≈ 2656

**∴ The compound interest for 2 years is **₹**2656.**
